resources.string: Android\'s own extra dim. Penombra does not keep running.
Android\'s own extra dim. Controlling it needs a permission given once from a computer. Until then Penombra uses the Eclipse.
Turn on USB debugging in Developer options, connect the phone to a computer with ADB and run this command. Then come back here.
On realme and OPPO, first also turn on «Disable permission monitoring», in Developer options too.
Some phones (realme) drop the extra dim while locked: Penombra then lays a veil there only. Uses a few more resources: an accessibility service stays on while the extra dim is on.
A black veil over the whole screen, for pitch dark. It runs a small service only while it is on.
A black veil over the whole screen. It needs the «Display over other apps» permission.
A black veil over the whole screen. Works right away: the moon and the levels above set it.
A black veil over the whole screen. Works right away, it only needs the «Display over other apps» permission: Penombra asks on the first tap.
Black veil over everything, for pitch dark

The top bar (clock, battery, notifications) stays bright: Android lets only an accessibility service cover it. To darken it too, turn on Penombra in Accessibility. If the switch is greyed out: App info › ⋮ › Allow restricted settings.
Turns Penombra on and off by itself, every night.
The tile is in Quick Settings
Moon: %1$s%2$s. Drag down to darken, up to lighten.
Stays visible while the dark veil is on

Only lays the Eclipse veil over the top bar (clock, battery, notifications), the bottom bar and the lock screen too. It does not read the screen and touches nothing. If Penombra has the permission given from a computer, it turns this on and off by itself together with the veil.
